 Report: Texas to give more first-team reps to QB KJ Lacey Jr., Arch Manning still expected to start
 Nick Kosko @ nickkosko59 55m 0 Share Share 
 Texas is expected to give more first-team reps to redshirt freshman QB KJ Lacey Jr. , per ESPN’s Pete Thamel, but Arch Manning is still the expected starter. The Longhorns take on Ole Miss at home this weekend.
 “Sources: Texas is expected to give an up-tick in first-team quarterback reps to redshirt freshman KJ Lacey Jr. this week in practice,” Thamel wrote on Twitter/X . “Arch Manning still projects as the Texas starter. The uptick in Lacey’s reps is a signal that Texas could replace Manning if he continues to struggle.”
 $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage 
 Texas is coming off their second straight loss to a previously unranked opponent, this time losing 27-24 to Florida at home. Manning struggled in the game, failing to top 200 yards passing and had zero yards rushing. He also fumbled in the game.
 In the loss to Florida, Manning was 14-of-20 passing for 173 yards and a touchdown, with a fumble, and ran for zero yards. In six games this year, Manning has 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, five interceptions, a 63.9% completion percentage, 102 rushing yards and no rushing scores.
 As far as Lacey is concerned, he has three game appearances since last year. He is 8-of-9 passing for 70 yards, so his action has been limited. But based on what Thamel wrote, Lacey might get a decent look at a potential start should Manning continue to struggle.
 As a member of the Class of 2025, Lacey was a four-star recruit out of Saraland (Ala,) High, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking . He was the No. 13 overall prospect in the state, the No. 18 quarterback in the class and the No. 237 overall prospect in the class.
 This report comes on the heels of head coach Steve Sarkisian addressing the future of Arch Manning under center this season following the loss to Florida. He didn’t single out his second-year starter, but he mentioned that “everything” is under evaluation.
 “Obviously we’re extremely disappointed,” Sarkisian  said postgame . “We didn’t play very good football today outside of the first quarter. We kind of bled out and ended up controlling the ball in the second half.
 “Our inability to be effective on first down, and our ability to convert short-down situations. Really was the snapshot of it all. Very disappointed, but we’ll work and get back. We’ve got a better team than how we’re playing right now. It’s my job to figure out how to get us to play closer to our potential.”
